about: Motion lab (docs/apcalc-spec.md section 6). The motions and every number live in calculus/assets/tools/math/motion-lab.js; motions and contexts unlock with their topics (velocity-given motions with Unit 8). Checked by scripts/lib/apcalc-tool-checks/motion-lab.mjs.
intro: A car on a straight road, with its position, velocity and acceleration graphs drawn from the same motion. Press Play or drag across the graphs. Where the car speeds up, the graphs are tinted; where it slows down, they are hatched; dashed lines mark where it turns around. With velocity given (Unit 8), watch the position build up as the area under the velocity graph.
howItWorks:
• Position given: $v(t) = x'(t)$ and $a(t) = v'(t)$, each from its formula (shown under Formulas & numbers).
  • Velocity given: $x(t) = x(0) + \int_0^t v(s)\,ds$. A formula is integrated numerically (adaptive Simpson), a graph of straight pieces exactly by triangles and trapezoids. Displacement is $\int v$; total distance is $\int |v|$, split where $v$ changes sign.
  • Speeding up where $v$ and $a$ have the same sign, slowing down where their signs differ. The sign of $a$ alone never decides it.
  • A change of direction needs $v$ to change sign. Where $v = 0$ and keeps its sign, the car only pauses.
  • The car's arrows are scaled to the motion's largest velocity and acceleration; the dots under it are where it was every quarter second, so close dots mean slow.
